<subject>Re: AgriIndia's Q2 Procurement Allocation</subject>
<body>
I think our discussion about an incremental charge applying to farmers of all contract tiers was with regard to our speculation on how the "new CTC" cost recovery mechanism would work, not Krishnapuram Farms.  I think the recovery mechanism is still speculation. There are many differing alternatives.

That's my recollection.


From: Thomas Gade on 28/05/2024 11:05 AM
To: Reyansh Krish
cc: Chakradhar Lala, Hardik D Pal, Nihal 
Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan 
Subject: RE: AgriIndia's Q2 Procurement Allocation

I've have talked to Chakradhar.  I think I just misunderstood.
</body>

Best,
Reyansh




	Thomas Gade 23/05/2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar 
Lala  cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika 
Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D 
Pal  Subject: RE: AgriIndia's Q2 Procurement Allocation


Chakradhar, Nihal Karan, Reyansh Krish and I were on a trip with Viraj Vyas last week.  I understood from Nihal that Viraj may believe that all farmers, including direct access, should pay the increase you mention.  Nihal?  This was encouraging from a litigation exposure standpoint because, to the extent all producers are treated alike, our DA farmers who were resourced to utility procurement cannot claim to have been disadvantaged by our action.  The converse is also true:  if they have to pay because they were put back on utility procurement they may try to pass that cost through to us.  To the extent that any increase is to pay back DWR for buying power 02/01/24–03/30/25, and those on DA are not required to pay this, Farm Partnerships could have a substantial exposure to its clients.   Maybe we need to modify our strategy to take this into account. -----Original Message-----
From:  Lala, Chakradhar  
Sent: Thursday, May 23, 2024 8:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas; 
Sangrur; Muzaffarpur; Stoness, Agmark Traders; Bakhshi, Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish, Reyansh
Subject: AgriIndia's Q2 Procurement Allocation


SDGE's AgriNet filing confirms that the ABX143 rate freeze of ₹6.50 does not apply to direct access.

In hearings on SDGE's potential rate increase for large suppliers:
SDGE has proposed to allocate all retained procurement to small farmers (below 100 kw equivalent).  Large farmers would be served  by DWR (or be direct access).  It's apparent several parties have major problems with this. It is interesting that SDGE has calculated the expected rate increase under their plan as ₹2.86.  If large farmers are allocated a piece of retained procurement, the increase goes up to ₹2.99.  In the latter case, large farmers retain a CTC (related to QF contracts and other long term stranded costs) that they would lose in the former case. Our involvement is to get an order 1) excluding DA from any rate increase (the proposed ₹2.86) 2) excluding DA from any surcharge related to undercollection from the rate freeze (an amount that is not known at this point) 3) prorating the surcharge related to undercollection if the customer
